title: The Seventh Year at the Lip

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The last tend keeps six where the house can count and one where it cannot; the river goes on with its note and does not stop for the hand that follows it.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the drying racks in the kiln month

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a two-hundred-and-one-to-three-day-old body carried everywhere and told by nobody — six months and twenty-one days to six months and twenty-three days, no roof with a word for it. The surgeon's register colours the noticing (a cost asked as a direction answered with the pot and the weather, a carrying arm as a record in muscle that knows weight and not cost, the private file turned out as instruments on a towel, likenesses taken down one at a time before they can stand up and call themselves a rule, and an inch of a small hand asked again under a roof the market cannot enter) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line — the old life stays offstage — and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector or back-room interior, no new hearing, no tenth stopping, no third gap, no fourth likeness made a cause, no seventh green, no seventh sighting, no calling of the loan, no payer named, no private record read and no ending

scenes.title: The Last Tend Opens Quiet
scenes.synopsis: First entry, first dated heading and drop capital: Day 201, Ember 22, Secondday, small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof, then before first grey and into the morning. No recap of the longest holding and no boundary drawn at the turn into the last tend. The count is carried at two hundred exact, complete and unspent (T071/T072); the boy is two hundred and one days old and six months and twenty-one days and nobody says so. First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool with the sour Ash breath of the unswept corner; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell. One leathery brown-edged crust lies two inches from his ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; the thread of drool is frozen and unwiped; cold has stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back, the afterdrop waiting on a warming nobody will perform. The carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for two hundred and one days (T088); through the finger's-width door the river keeps its note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings; overhead the boards keep four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — three counts in three places that do not become one, because a man who wanted them to agree would have to put a payer under all three and none stands to any (T061/T082). Sella gives every instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket, says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without a touch, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, feeds him from the house's own dish with the spoon on her sleeve and his mouth unwiped, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with her hand resting a half-beat longer at the setting, and leaves the widow's mark untouched, for there has been no opening since before the kiln on Ember 1 (T058/T079). A neighbour's cost-question about what the firing will want now the last tend is in goes to the pot and the weather and away level, nothing priced or entered (T077). Three or four men unnamed go low into the back room before first grey and get no name and no third telling (T035/T031/T065/T095). In the morning the hand goes up an inch toward the note through the door and comes down at once, with no holding in it — the asking is not always answered — and is filed on a sixth place of its own, not a hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, one of the three held changes, key, power or rule, no payer named and nothing stood up out of it. End: two hundred and one stands exact in the wool, unspent, spoken by nobody; the last tend has opened as an ordinary morning.

scenes.title: What the Afternoon Kept
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 201, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; heat goes off the high air first and stays longest under the shelf, behind the pot and in the fold of wool, and the underside of the shelf makes a roof that stops at the edge of his reach. Sella stands with her back to the basket, moves her lips along a row with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal tally stays unread, uncounted and uncopied, and tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it where another woman would say I, stands with the back of the pot counting under her breath toward no opening and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079, T100). At the kindling the knife lies at the edge of its sill with six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it; Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, and sweeps the collector's road without turning — no collector comes. Chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, pale clip-ring at the left wrist; the ear-sentence comes to the word that would call the loan and stops with no figure and no name, the Seed 16 breath is drawn and not spent, nine stoppings stay nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the seventh year stands nearer its end than ever and has not given, the loan is uncalled, and the stroke goes over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check (T036/T076). At the wheel-shed Jorra gives the men no name and does not say the room was cold, brings fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note three turns ahead and withholds it from a man come up on a wrong wind whose saying about a pot singing early stays a saying and whose pot is not lost (T035/T031, T061/T082). When Sella's voice goes low and unfinished his bent finger goes into the cold damper and holds until the sentence reaches the pot, then the tongue moves a hair's breadth and the finger is left standing — a remembered repetition, not a change made again, not paired with the Day 161, 166 or 171 fractions; the iron is one piece with two bites, with no word in Grathic for both mercies, joined to no kiln and entered in no slate (T062). He's not Vail stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name to the slate-burners stays ungiven. At the going of the light Sella carries him home up the clay road, instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, woodsmoke in long low bars before her and river wind behind with the taste of water over water, the two passing without taking each other's colour; the arm that has carried him two hundred and one mornings keeps the height of the handle, the give of the shoulder and the turn of the wrist at a step's end, a record in muscle that remembers weight and not cost. She goes wide around the pan's gone round ring, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098). Under the roof she sets him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without looking at his face and leaves the thread frozen; the two rooms do not touch. In the small hours the file is turned out as instruments on a towel, exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth out of a person and no seventh invented, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, told bell beside heard and told figure beside paid, three held changes on three places with the loft scrape on a fourth and the pale line on a fifth, nine stoppings with no tenth, crust's gap and two shelf gaps and pan's gone ring and field's empty place on trays that do not touch, charcoal unread, stone cold in its loft pot, Seed 16 breath unspent, loan uncalled, cost of the man carried out entered nowhere (T061/T082, T006, T064, T060/T086/T097, T100). The hand goes up an inch and holds for the length of the small intake only and comes down before the letting go; it is filed on the sixth place beside the others and not laid across them. End: the hand down against the fold and the count going forward.

scenes.title: The Cost Asked as a Direction
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 202, Ember 23, Thirdday, small hours under the Vail roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf, the yard well and the edge of the clay road. The boy is two hundred and two days old and six months and twenty-two days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth has had no payer for two hundred and two days (T088); river, fire and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). First smell hot clay under tallow and wet wool under that; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap. The sweet edge of lead glaze comes up off High Kiln on a wrong wind and goes out on the same wrong wind, answered as a direction and entered nowhere; the saying that a pot singing before its time generally sings itself out early stays a saying about a pot and is not made true as a lesson (T064 held). Sella's instruction goes to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket; she says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar without a touch, feeds him from the house's own dish with the spoon on her sleeve, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat at the setting, and does not touch the widow's mark, because a morning and a shelf are not openings and there has been no opening since Ember 1 (T058/T079). At the yard well a rack woman with slip dried pale in the creases of her wrists asks what the pots will want before the kiln month is out and is told to ask the pot and the weather; a man come off the clay road with a number in his fist asks what the kiln will want now the figure has gone up twice and is answered with the house and the weather. Both cost-questions go away level, nothing priced, refused or entered (T077). The second reading of Ember stays offstage and unchallenged: Berr's box went up the road locked with the true subtraction inside, the figure was read twice over the basket and is still not the figure paid, Hessa's slate lies unread at Greybank with the writing to her sleeve, and the soft-cuffed clerk is still set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called (T015/T041/T047, T080, T090 held). The market does not get to read the inch. Back under the roof the hand goes up an inch toward the note through the door and comes down before the counted breath has finished — a shorter holding, the body keeping its own time, an inch let go early and no failure in it — filed on its sixth place, not a hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, change, key, power or rule, with no payer named (T061/T082). He still cannot close the two inches, lift the crust or speak a number. End: two hundred and two stands exact in the wool, complete and unspent, spoken by nobody.

scenes.title: The Holding Remembered
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 202, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the hearth, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending; heat stays longest in the low places under the shelf, behind the pot and in the fold where one brown-edged crust lies leathery two inches from the ear with its empty place unnamed and no third, the thread frozen and unwiped, cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist joint, the afterdrop waiting. Sella moves her lips along a row standing with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, keeps her finger from beneath the front edge so the charcoal stays unread, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting, and does not look toward the bed — she never looks toward the bed at the setting (T058/T079, T100). The widow's mark hangs where it hung, touched once before the kiln on Ember 1 and at no other hour. At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after its instruction, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while keeping the late because it puts off the paying, brings the ear-sentence all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it; nine stoppings stand as nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the Seed 16 breath is unspent, the loan is uncalled, the seventh year presses nearer its end and has still not given, and his stroke goes over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check and over the collector's road without turning, no collector coming. Ash stays worked into his knuckle creases, the pale clip-ring holds what light there is, his chest has been tight since the dark, and Garl's unforged collector sentence lies beside the knife (T036/T076). At the wheel-shed Jorra keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot You'll do, withholds its full note from a wrong-wind man whose saying stays a saying and no pot is lost, and when Sella's voice goes low and unfinished puts his bent finger into the cold damper and holds until the sentence reaches the pot, then leaves it standing a hair's breadth moved — a remembered repetition and not a new change, read as one iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both, joined to no kiln and entered in no slate (T035/T031/T062, T065/T095). He's not Vail stays sealed and the promise stays ungiven. At the going of the light Sella carries him home at the half-pace, woodsmoke before her in long low bars and river wind behind with the taste of water over water, the arm keeping its record of weight and not cost; she goes wide around the pan's gone ring, the bare dark trough, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098). Under the roof: the bed and not the Debt Loft, fold right without a look at his face, thread left frozen, fire answering four low pulls with the fifth missing and its payer unnamed for two hundred and two days, river's fifth low note through the door, boards' four nails, four and a knot — three counts that do not become one (T088, T061/T082). In the small hours the file is laid out again, exact, complete and worth nothing; the hand goes up an inch, stays up through the whole of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire in the room that does not touch his, and comes down with the breath rather than before it — the old coordination remembered, not a longer reach, not a new change, not promoted into a hearing or a rule, filed on its sixth place beside the others and never laid across them (T061/T082). End: the fold takes the hand without a word and nothing is joined, named, opened, called, spent or ended.

scenes.title: Two Hundred and Three
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 203, Ember 24, Fourthday, small hours under the Vail roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf, the kindling and the edge of the yard. The kiln month's last tend runs into its third day with no boundary drawn and no shift in the district's two names for the months. The boy is two hundred and three days old and six months and twenty-three days and nobody says so (T071/T072); the carried fire's payer is unnamed for two hundred and three days (T088); fire, river and boards keep three counts in three places that do not become one (T061/T082). Sella's instruction goes where it always goes — to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom, the running water and the river wind, never to the basket — and she says the house, keeps her half-pace, glances once at the clay jar without a touch, feeds him from the house's own dish with the spoon on her sleeve and not his mouth, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat at the setting, tells the fire it is the thaw, and leaves the widow's mark where it hangs, because a morning and a shelf are not openings and there has been no opening since Ember 1 (T058/T079). A cost-question brought to the door goes to the pot and the weather and away level, nothing entered (T077). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it has been told its work, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to the ones who want the thaw early and the ones who want it late, agrees so entirely that no argument can find a foot and keeps wanting the late because a late thaw puts off the paying, though the paying has stood in the ruts since the water went; the small knife lies at the edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged sentence beside it; the ear-sentence comes to his teeth and no further with no figure and no name, the ninth stopping is not made a tenth before the seventh year is earned, the Seed 16 breath is unspent and the loan uncalled (T036/T076). Three or four men unnamed have gone low into the back room before first grey and Jorra has come through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger, given them no name and said nothing about the room; the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third (T035/T031/T065/T095). In the morning the hand goes up an inch toward the note through the finger's-width door and holds for the length of the small intake only, then comes down before the letting go — the answer the body gives on this morning — filed on its sixth place beside the others, not a hearing, seventh, stopping, payment, one of the three held changes, key, power or rule, no payer named and nothing made of it (T061/T082). He still cannot close the two inches to the pot handle, lift the crust two inches to his mouth or speak a number. End: two hundred and three stands exact in the wool, complete and unspent, spoken by nobody under any roof.

scenes.title: The Hand and the River
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 203, Ember 24, Fourthday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf, the hearth, the kindling, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed. The afternoon thins without ending, heat going off the high air first and staying longest under the shelf, behind the pot and in the fold of wool where the one leathery crust lies two inches from the ear with its empty place unnamed and no third; thread of drool frozen and unwiped; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist joint, the afterdrop waiting. Sella stands with her back to the basket, moves her lips along the row with two unnamed gaps and gives nobody a figure, glances once at the clay jar and shuts her hand half over nothing without a touch, keeps her finger from beneath the shelf so the charcoal stays unread, tells the fire it is the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says The house will keep it, stands with the back of the pot counting under her breath toward no opening — small intake, hold, letting go — pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, lets her hand rest a half-beat longer at the setting, and does not look toward the bed (T058/T079, T100). The widow's mark is untouched at a dusk, for a dusk is not an opening. At the kindling the knife lies at the very edge of its sill, six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it; Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood Six counted. The next I don't count, says Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, brings the ear-sentence all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, draws the breath he should have spent and does not spend it, keeps nine stoppings as nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned, the seventh year nearer its end than ever and still not given with the word on the other side of his teeth, the Seed 16 breath unspent and the loan uncalled; his stroke goes over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check and over the collector's road without turning, and no collector comes; Ash is worked into his knuckles, the pale clip-ring holds what light there is, his chest has been tight since the dark (T036/T076). At the wheel-shed Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip, keeps dusty and clean forearms on one tray, asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, speaks to the wheel before anyone, tells a pot You'll do, knows its full note three turns ahead and withholds it from a wrong-wind man whose saying about a pot singing early stays a saying about a pot and whose pot is not lost (T035/T031, T061/T082). When Sella's voice goes low and unfinished his bent finger goes into the cold damper ahead of his hand and holds until the sentence reaches the pot, then the tongue moves a hair's breadth and the finger is left standing — a remembered repetition, not a change made again, not paired with the Day 161, 166 or 171 fractions; the iron is one piece with two bites, the holding and the taking, with no word in Grathic for both mercies, joined to no kiln and entered in no slate, and the two shut-room tellings stay two with no third (T062, T065/T095). He's not Vail stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name to the slate-burners stays ungiven. At the going of the light she carries him home at the half-pace, instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket, woodsmoke in long low bars before her and river wind behind with the taste of water over water, the two passing without taking each other's colour, the arm keeping its record of weight and not cost; she goes wide around the pan's gone round ring, the bare dark trough whose water is called weather, the rack space with its broken birth-slates, the field's empty place and the place the carriers crossed, each with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098). Under the roof she sets him on the bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right without a look at his face, leaves the thread frozen; the fire answers four low pulls with the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for two hundred and three days; through the finger's-width door the river keeps its fifth low note and overhead the boards keep four nails, four and a thumb-width knot — three counts in three places that do not become one (T088, T061/T082). In the small hours he turns out the file as a man lays instruments on a towel, exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with the sixth out of a person and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and unpaid, told bell beside heard and told figure beside paid with the second reading gone up the road in Berr Clay's locked box and still not the figure paid, Hessa Rale's slate unread at Greybank and the soft-cuffed clerk still set at the landing for an uncalled measure, three held changes on three places with the loft scrape on a fourth and the pale line on a fifth, nine stoppings with no tenth, crust's gap and two shelf gaps and pan's gone ring and field's empty place on trays that do not touch, no third gap, no fourth likeness, no finger drawn, charcoal unread, stone cold in its loft pot, Seed 16 breath unspent, loan uncalled, cost of the man carried out entered nowhere, sixth green still a colour and foundling still a shape (T061/T082, T006, T064, T060/T086/T097, T100, T078, T015/T041/T047, T080, T090, T050/T051, T033/T034). Then he puts the question to his hand. It goes up an inch toward the note of water over water through the door, stays through the small intake, the hold and the letting go of one of the breaths Sella counts at her fire in the room that does not touch his, and this time does not come down with her breath: it keeps the small height through the little silence after her count has ended and comes down on the river's next low note — a coordination with a second rhythm, uncounted and ungiven, not a longer reach, not a stronger hand, not a hearing, not a seventh, not a stopping, not a payment, not one of the three held changes, not a key, not a power and not a rule, no payer named and nothing stood up out of it, filed on the sixth place beside the others and never laid across them (T061/T082, advanced and not paid). He still cannot close the two inches, lift the crust or speak a number; the river goes on without noticing that an inch rode it for the length of one note. End: the hand down against the fold on the river's note, two hundred and three standing exact in the dark, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody, the seventh year nearer its end than ever and still not given, the count going forward into Day 204, Ember 25, Fifthday.
